w10_T4_002437: Liam started the day with 76 stickers in his collection. In the morning he traded some cards and gained 15 more stickers. By midday he had found another 25 stickers stuck inside an old notebook. In the afternoon, he gave away 93 stickers to classmates for a school project. In the evening, his aunt surprised him with 25 more stickers as a gift. How many stickers does Liam have now?
w10_T4_002440: Sara had $105 saved from her allowance. She earned $64 more helping neighbors with yard work last weekend. Then she spent $77 on a new bicycle helmet. Sara had far more money than her friend Tom, who only had $50 saved up. For her good grades, a relative gave her a bonus that made her savings 3 times as large as before. Sara then divided that money evenly between 2 accounts, one for herself and one for her sister, and kept only her own share. How much money did Sara keep in her own account?
w10_T4_002446: A vending machine's coin box held 163 cents at the start of the school day. During morning cleanup, the janitor removed 93 cents to fix a jammed slot. He then split what remained evenly between 2 identical collection jars and kept only one jar. That afternoon, the office manager added 58 cents in cafeteria change to the jar, and later the school store contributed another 56 cents. For the bank deposit, the treasurer made 8 identical envelopes, each holding that same jar amount, and combined them into one total. Since 100 cents equal 1 dollar, the school always double-checked its coin counts. How many cents did the treasurer send to the bank?
w10_T4_002447: A young gymnast began the week with 52 practice points on her scorecard. Early in the morning session, her coach awarded her 62 more points for perfect landings. By midmorning, 51 points were deducted after she missed a routine. That afternoon, a scoring bonus made her total 5 times as large as it had been. Later, in the evening session, a second bonus round made her new total another 5 times as large again. Since the gym recorded points in tenths and rounded them to whole points at day's end, no fractions ever appeared on the chart. Finally, right before the night's final tally, a completion award added 71 more points. What was the gymnast's final point total?
w10_T4_002449: Before dawn, a shipping warehouse loaded 7 trucks, each carrying 177 identical crates of oranges, onto the loading dock. In the morning, workers unloaded 516 crates to fill an order for a downtown grocery chain. By the afternoon, an inspection found 641 crates had spoiled in the heat and had to be thrown out. In the evening, a late delivery from a nearby farm added 13 more crates to the dock. How many crates of oranges remained on the dock by night?
w10_T4_002452: Maya started her trading card collection with 14 cards. She then received 75 more cards from a booster pack her cousin gave her. Maya's friend Diego bragged that his own collection was smaller, with only 9 cards to his name. A store promotion made Maya's total grow to 4 times its size after she completed a rare set. She later traded away 105 cards to a collector for a signed poster. After the school card fair, she gave up another 231 cards to settle a bet she'd lost. How many cards does Maya have left?
w10_T4_002454: A phone's battery showed 88 percent charge when Nina left for her hike. During the first hour, streaming music drained 29 percent. Taking photos on a scenic overlook used another 22 percent. A long phone call on the way down cost her 36 percent more. Since her phone reports charge in percent, which is just battery-minutes converted to a fraction of 100, she never worried about the raw units. When she got home, her charger's fast-charge mode brought her battery up to 6 times its drained level before bed. Overnight, a scheduled optimization further pushed it to 5 times that amount by morning. What percent charge did Nina's phone show the next morning?
w10_T4_002466: Before sunrise, a candy factory prepared 8 identical pallets, each stacked with 173 boxes of chocolate bars, for the day's shipment. In the morning, workers added 8 more boxes found in a storage room. By midday, the shipment was split evenly across 3 delivery trucks, and only one truck's load continued on to the client. That afternoon, the client's receiving clerk, who happened to keep a dozen spare pallets on hand just in case, added 11 more boxes from a backup crate. In the evening, a return shipment brought back 29 boxes sent to the wrong address, and since the factory logs inventory by converting bulk cases into individual boxes for its ledger, the final number always had to be exact. Overnight, a regional distribution order required 4 times that evening total to be packed for the next day. How many boxes were packed for the regional shipment?
w10_T4_002469: A community garden plot had 40 tomato plants at the start of spring. Volunteers added 15 more seedlings in early April. A donation from a local nursery brought in 65 additional plants in May. By June, the garden had grown by 32 more plants thanks to a seed-sharing event. When the harvest was divided evenly among 4 neighborhood families, only one family's share continued to be tracked for the community log. That family then lost 6 plants to a late blight. How many tomato plants did that family end up with?
w10_T4_002471: A bakery started the morning with 45 loaves of sourdough bread on the shelf. By midmorning, 11 loaves had been sold to early customers. In the afternoon, the ovens finished a new batch, adding 38 more loaves to the shelf. That evening, a wholesale order required 9 times the afternoon total to be prepared for a chain of cafes. Overnight, the shipment was split evenly among 3 delivery vans. How many loaves did each van carry?
w10_T4_002474: On a fishing trip, Owen caught 20 fish by mid-morning. In the afternoon, a sudden storm forced him to release 15 fish back into the lake. He then split his remaining catch evenly into 5 coolers to keep them fresh, and only tracked one cooler's fish for the weigh-in. Later that evening, a friend gave him 4 times as many fish as were in that cooler. Before heading home for the night, 1 fish flopped back into the water. How many fish did Owen bring home?
w10_T4_002477: The school library shelf held 66 mystery novels at the start of the term. A dozen students donated their personal comic books to a separate donation bin that the library hadn't sorted yet. During the first month, the library received 56 new mystery novels from a publisher. A local author then donated 18 more signed copies. By the semester's midpoint, a book fair added 6 more novels to the shelf. Right before finals week, the librarian found 74 additional novels in a storage closet. How many mystery novels were on the shelf by finals week?
w10_T4_002479: A charity jar held 20 dollars in donations at the start of the fundraiser morning. By midday, the treasurer split the jar evenly between 2 charity boxes and kept tracking only one box, ignoring the 200 raffle tickets that had gone unsold. In the afternoon, a generous donor added 73 dollars to that box. That evening, a matching-donation program grew the box's total to 5 times its size. Overnight, processing fees shrank it back down to one-fifth of that amount by morning, and since 100 cents make 1 dollar, the bank always rounded exactly to the cent. Finally, 82 dollars had to be paid out the next day for venue costs. How much money was left in the box?
w10_T4_002486: A runner logged 62 minutes of training time on Monday. On Tuesday, an injury forced her to cut back, losing 56 minutes from her weekly total. Her coach then required her to make up for it by training for 7 times as long as what remained. On Wednesday, she added 40 more minutes for a recovery jog. Since her coach preferred tracking sessions in hours rather than raw minutes, converting every 60 minutes into 1 hour on the log, the team still recorded exact minutes for precision. By the end of the week, a bonus endurance session made her total grow to 3 times its size. How many minutes of training did the runner log by the end of the week?
w10_T4_002490: A parking garage had 176 cars parked at opening time in the morning. By midmorning, 39 more cars pulled in, though the tour bus company, which normally reserved a dozen spots just for its own buses, wasn't part of this count. At midday, 8 additional cars arrived for a lunch rush. In the afternoon, 187 cars left for a downtown event. By evening, 17 more cars departed as offices closed. Late at night, 56 more cars pulled in for a concert. How many cars were in the garage at the end of the night?
w10_T4_002491: A stamp collector owned 223 stamps in his album at the beginning of the year. In spring, he traded away 193 stamps to a fellow collector for a rare set. He then lost 2 stamps when a page got damaged in a move. Over the summer, an estate sale added 42 more stamps to his collection. In the fall, a museum donation brought in 52 additional stamps. A national exhibition award then grew his entire collection to 9 times its size. Afterward, he gave half of that award collection to his nephew to start his own hobby, keeping the rest for himself. How many stamps did the collector keep?
w10_T4_002492: Priya scored 154 points in the first round of a video game tournament. A double-points power-up she picked up made her round total grow to 2 times its size. She then lost 64 points when a hidden trap wiped out part of her combo streak. Her rival, Jonas, had scored far fewer points overall and was already out of contention for the finals. In the bonus round, Priya earned 3 more points for a perfect combo. A final multiplier event for the top players made her total grow to 8 times its size. What was Priya's final score?
w10_T4_002503: Farmer Ellen collected 134 eggs from her henhouse on Monday, and by Tuesday morning, 6 more eggs had been laid overnight. By Wednesday, a new batch of hens added 61 more eggs to her count, far more than her neighbor Farmer Curtis managed to collect from his own flock all week. On Thursday, Ellen's total grew by 80 more eggs after she bought extra hens from another farm. On Friday, 33 eggs were lost when a carton broke during transport. Heading into the weekend, a bulk order required 9 times her Friday total, and a second regional order right after that required 5 times that new amount. How many eggs did Ellen need to supply for the final order?
w10_T4_002510: Priya's jar held 225 coins at the start of summer, far more than her cousin Wesley's much smaller jar. She added 5 more coins she found under her couch cushions. She then spent 106 coins on a toy at the arcade, ignoring her grandmother's separate collection of foreign coins from over 40 different countries. Priya divided her remaining coins evenly across 4 piggy banks and kept tracking just one. A prize drawing then grew that piggy bank's total to 5 times its size. Finally, she added 3 more coins she earned for chores. How many coins were in that piggy bank?
w10_T4_002511: A bookshop owner named Delia had 198 novels in stock at the start of the month, considerably more than Frank's shop across the street. She sold off 161 novels during a clearance sale. A surprise bestseller then doubled her remaining stock overnight. A publisher's restock event made that new total grow to 4 times its size. She then received 80 more novels from a donation drive. Finally, a local author dropped off 38 more signed copies. How many novels did Delia have in stock by the end of the month?
w10_T4_002514: A water tank held 236 liters at the start of the week. A rainstorm added 22 more liters on Monday. On Tuesday, a small leak was patched after adding just 6 more liters from a backup supply. By Wednesday, farmers drew out 162 liters for irrigation. The remaining water was then split evenly between 2 identical tanks, and only one tank continued to be monitored. Since the farm's gauge reads in liters but the co-op reports totals in gallons, workers always converted the numbers in their logs before submitting reports. On Thursday, a delivery truck added 67 more liters to the monitored tank. How many liters were in that tank by the end of Thursday?
w10_T4_002515: Two hikers, Ana and Beto, set out on a long trail together, though Beto, who carried a dozen extra water bottles, ended up hiking far less than Ana that day. Ana climbed 168 meters up the first slope before stopping to rest. A rockslide forced her to backtrack 66 meters to find a safer path. She then climbed a steep section that was 5 times as long as what remained after the backtrack. Since the trail markers were posted in meters but the park's map used kilometers, Ana always converted her count before checking her position. Near the summit, she covered 64 more meters along a ridge, and a short detour around a fallen tree added 21 more meters to her hike. How many meters had Ana hiked in total?
w10_T4_002523: A concession stand run by Rosa started the game with 206 hot dogs in stock, far more than Jake's rival stand kept on hand nearby. During the first quarter, 153 hot dogs were sold. A halftime rush meant Rosa had to prepare 7 times as many hot dogs as what was left, pulling extra stock from the freezer. Over the third quarter, 264 hot dogs were sold to the crowd. By the fourth quarter, 90 more hot dogs were sold before the stand closed. How many hot dogs were left unsold at closing?
w10_T4_002530: At dawn, a charity walk-a-thon began with 7 teams, each pledging to raise 46 dollars for every mile completed as a base pledge. By morning, 6 more dollars had been pledged by a walk-up donor. At midday, a local business added 52 dollars to the fund. In the afternoon, a matching-donation drive brought in 29 more dollars. By evening, a final surge of last-minute donations added 26 more dollars. How much money had the walk-a-thon raised by evening?
w10_T4_002534: At sunrise, a baker prepared 9 identical trays, each holding 33 cookies, for the morning market stall. By mid-morning, a wholesale buyer required 4 times that tray total for a large event order. At midday, the baker added 21 more cookies from a fresh batch. By afternoon, a second event doubled the midday total for an extra order. Finally, in the evening, a citywide festival required 8 times that afternoon total to supply every booth. How many cookies did the baker need to supply the festival?
